title: Volume 1 Chapter 1: Nail Chip 3
content: Don't make that face.
You’re smiling, but you look like you’re about to cry.
Not being able to do nails—that’s all it is—but for Sayori Goto, it’s an incredibly frustrating and unreasonable situation.
“I’m really sorry for barging in and asking for so much! But I’m sure we’ll find a good way to do this, so I’m not giving up!”
Before I could say anything.
No, maybe she was trying to prevent me from saying anything. The positive dragon girl probably didn’t want to hear any more about “impossible” or “can’t do it.”
She seemed to be convincing herself that a good solution would be found.
“Well then, Azuma-kun! See you at school!”
Just like that, Sayori Goto, who had suddenly come to my garage, left with the same energy she had when she arrived.
After Sayori went home, I was left alone, organizing my tools.
I regretted saying something like that.
(Finding a solution isn’t going to be easy...)
Dealing with those nails that couldn’t form a coating wasn’t something that could be done easily.

That’s why Sayori Goto had been turned away from many nail salons. Even after that experience, she still couldn’t give up and came to someone like me, who had little connection to her, just because I was good at model making.
Because of that...
When I expressed my doubts, she tried to cover it up with a smile, almost on the verge of tears.
(What an idiot I am...)
What does “impossible” even mean?
I looked at the display of models I had made in the garage.
There were dioramas recreating scenes from anime, original robot designs that didn’t appear in any anime, and kits that had been mixed together.
When I envisioned making these, I also thought, “This might be impossible.” After all, each of them had a high level of difficulty in modification and painting.
Even so, I piled up my skills and knowledge, worked diligently, and once I sprayed the final clear coat, the models I thought were impossible to make were somehow completed.
Of course, I still feel there are areas that are insufficient, and I believe I can improve their quality even more.
But in that way, I had somehow overcome the impossible.
Model making—creating in general—isn’t that what it’s all about?
(I’ve already taken on the challenge...)
To be honest, it didn’t have to be a plastic model to create three-dimensional objects.
I naturally got into model making because I liked anime, games, and robots—but...
In reality, as long as I could feel the sense of accomplishment from creating something, it didn’t have to be a robot model. It could be a tank or a castle.
If my hobbies had been slightly different, I might have been sculpting with clay or painting. Or maybe sewing. In any case...
I love bringing the images that exist only in my mind into reality.
So then...
(Nails are the same, right...?)
Sayori Goto must have her ideal nails.
I don’t know how close I can get to that, but to make it happen, I need to build up my knowledge and skills.
I don’t know much about nails, but I do have knowledge and skills when it comes to models. If I use those, I can definitely overcome the impossible.
(Think, research)
I picked up my smartphone and started searching for information about nails.
If filing her nails is impossible, I have to find another way.
There’s no doubt my knowledge can be applied.
After all, nails and plastic models are similar. Even just today, while filing and painting Sayori’s nails, there were many aspects where model-making techniques could be utilized.
(There has to be something... absolutely...)
The tools are all in the garage.
As for materials, I have junk parts, plastic sheets, and even some metal parts.
If I need paint, I can express any color. I’ve been using an airbrush for ten years.
And so, in the garage, I began sliding through the colorful search results for nails one after another.
(I’ll figure something out. I’ll make her nails... I will create them.)
I want to make what had only existed in my imagination with my own hands.
That desire, which I had previously used for my own model-making, I want to use now, just for Sayori Goto.
I couldn’t forgive the fact that such a positive, bright, seemingly flawless girl was looking so close to tears.
Changing the search terms one after another, my smartphone displayed details about nails. Eventually, my eyes landed on a particular phrase.
It was a word I had never heard before, but for some reason, it stood out and easily entered my mind.
“...Nail Chip?”
From that day on.
As soon as school ended, I started heading straight to the garage.
There had been times before when I got so absorbed in model making that I locked myself in the garage, so my family didn’t say anything.
My father, who lent me the garage, would only say, “Don’t stay out too late” and “Make sure to eat your meals.”
When my father got busy with work, he would also retreat to the garage to paint cars. He probably understood the feeling of getting absorbed in a task.
I was going to make Sayori’s nails.
After deciding that, I immersed myself in the work without distraction. Fortunately, all the tools were in the garage, and I could accurately envision the steps to completion.
Cutting out materials. Shaping. Polishing. Surface treatment. Painting.
I would repurpose a design I had planned to use for a robot’s paint job someday.
(For her nails...)
For several days, I focused solely on making the nails.
There were times when my eyes met Sayori’s in class, but—there were no conversations. Since I had said that nails were impossible, I didn’t know what to talk about.
I just thought that as long as I could hand over the finished product, that would be enough.
Sayori could indeed have nails. She should be able to have the nails she envisioned. If she could understand that it was absolutely not impossible—then that would be enough for me.
So, for the past few days, I had been holed up in the garage after school.
As long as I could envision the process and the final product, all that was left was to create it—I wasn’t just a casual modeler; I had been doing this since childhood.
I smoothly reached the point of completion.
“Phew...”
About an hour after finishing the final clear coat, I looked at the completed products lined up in the painting booth.
(Well, it’s more like a plastic model than nails...)
I could just put them in a plastic case I bought at a hundred yen shop and hand them to Sayori tomorrow.
I wondered what kind of face she would make—if possible, I wanted her to be happy. That’s what I thought.
“—Huh?”
The entrance to the garage swung open with force.
“Hey! Why haven’t you replied to my messages? You haven’t even read them! ...Huh? Are you wearing a mask?”
“Wait, wait, hold on...”
I had a lot to say, but for now...
“I was just painting, so... could you wait outside?”
“Ah!? You were making models!? Sorry!”
When painting, make sure to ventilate and wear a mask.
Even though the paint booth for models provides sufficient ventilation, it’s still not good for someone to suddenly come in without a mask.
“I’ll clean up a bit! It’ll be done soon!”
“Okay! Once you’re done, I have a lot to say!”
What does she want to say?
Could it be that she’s angry because I ended up abandoning the project halfway through after having taken it on?
I picked up the “completed product” that I had just painted.
I would have preferred to let it dry a bit longer, but it couldn’t be helped. I never expected Sayori to burst in like this.
What should I say when I hand this over?
As I cleaned up my tools, I kept thinking about that.
“...Thanks for waiting.”
“I waited!”
After about ten minutes, I was finally able to call Sayori into the garage.
Just like before, we faced each other across the work desk.
For some reason, Sayori had her arms crossed and was puffing out her chest.
It was a pose that clearly said, “I’m angry.”
Since her uniform was unbuttoned at the chest, her ample bosom was emphasized. I wished she would stop that.
The tip of her tail had been tapping the floor repeatedly. I wondered if that was also a sign of her displeasure.
“So—uh, why did you come so suddenly?”
“Why not!? Didn’t you see my messages!? After that, I did some research on my own and sent it to you, but you didn’t reply at all!”
“Huh?”
I hurriedly pulled out my smartphone.
I had about thirty unread messages from Sayori.

“I found this when I researched nails!” “This color is cute!” “Hey, give me a reply!” “Did you not see it?” “...Are you mad?” “I want to do this nail!” “Hey, ignoring me hurts!” “I’m coming to the garage now!” “I’m seriously going to barge in!”
It was a flood of messages.
Since I hardly ever used the app, I hadn’t even checked them.
“...Sorry, I had notifications turned off because I wanted to focus on my work.”
“Huh!? I was super worried because you didn’t reply at all!? You were just ignoring me!?”
“I don’t usually use messaging apps...”
“Change your settings in front of me! Right now! Immediately! It’s a problem if there’s an emergency!”
Would there really be urgent communication between us?
I wondered about that, but for now, I turned on the notifications to calm Sayori down.
“Just a word is enough to ease my worries, so please reply!”
“Y-Yeah, I’ll be careful...”
Even though it wasn’t intentional, ignoring her might not have been the best idea.
“But... I thought you wouldn’t ask me anymore.”
“Eh!? Why not!?”
“You said you felt bad about taking up my time...”
“Well, of course! If it takes an hour to do nails! That’s why I said we should look for a way and parted ways!”
“Huh? ...Does that mean we were supposed to search for a solution together?”
“That’s what I said!”
Sayori’s eyes widened.
“Did I... say something wrong? Did I say something weird?”
“No, um—maybe I was overthinking it. Since I said it was impossible, I thought you wouldn’t ask for nails anymore.”
“No, no, no! You’re the one I rely on!”
Sayori let out a big sigh and leaned back against the folding chair.

“I felt like you were avoiding me for the past few days, and you didn’t talk to me at school, and whenever I tried to talk to you, you left right away... I was wondering why! But it turns out you weren’t avoiding me.”
“Ah, sorry. I was just busy working...”
Also, talking at school was still a high hurdle for me.
“Ugh, I’m sorry if I made you feel bad! But you need time to make your models too, right?”
“No, what I was making wasn’t models.”
“Huh?”
I pulled out the completed product that I had just finished.
What was lined up on the work desk were thin plastic chips, ten pieces in a set. In other words...
“Is this... a nail chip?”
“Yeah.”
I nodded.

It seemed that nails weren’t just about applying paint to the nails. Sometimes, various decorations were applied to nail-shaped chips, which were then attached to the nails with glue. That’s what nail chips are.
After researching, I found out that the material for nail chips is plastic, so I judged that I could process and create them too.
“Wow, they’re shaped just like my nails!?”
“I just layered plastic sheets, shaped them with a file, and painted them. I could do this kind of processing in about three days.”
“Wow, Azuma-kun, you’re a genius!?”
“That’s a bit much.”
I had observed the shape and length of Sayori’s nails thoroughly the other day, so I remembered them well enough. I could process the plastic to match that shape.
—But if I said I remembered the shape of her nails, that would sound a bit creepy. I’ll keep that to myself.
“Ah, but my nails don’t hold glue...”
I thought so.
There’s no way Sayori, who is particular about nails, wouldn’t have considered the easy option of nail chips.
When she mentioned glue the other day, it probably meant she had tried nail chips and they didn’t work.
“Don’t worry. Just try it on.”
“Huh, try it on... what about glue or tape?”
“You don’t need any. Just place it on your nail.”
I looked straight into Sayori’s eyes and nodded. I was confident in my creation—Sayori Goto’s nail chips.
Just like the models I was proud of lined up on the shelf.
“Okay, I got it.”
Sayori, still a bit nervous about the potential for failure, cautiously placed the nail chip on her middle finger.
With a satisfying snap, like model parts fitting together, the nail chip clicked firmly onto Sayori’s nail.
“Huh!? What!? The chip stuck!?”
“I embedded a magnet.”
“A magnet!? Inside the chip!?”
It was amusing to see Sayori looking back and forth between me and the chip in a panic.
“I sometimes use small magnets when making models. They’re tiny, just enough to sit on the tip of a pinky finger. Since Sayori’s nails contain iron, I thought they would stick well with the magnet.”
“Sure enough! It fits perfectly!”
Using small magnets is common for parts of robot exteriors or weapons where frequent removal is desired.
Since I had used them a few times in the past, I had some leftover small magnets lying around in the storage.
If I embedded a magnet while layering the plastic sheets, I’d have completed Sayori’s custom magnetic nail chips.
“I used pretty strong magnets, so it’s best to keep them in a case and only attach them when needed.”
“You made this... for me?”
“Yeah, well.”
“Even though you said it was impossible...”
“Because I thought it was impossible—I looked for a way to do it with the skills I have. It’s not a proper nail chip, but still...”
I chose my words carefully.
Because she relied on me. Because I took it on. Because I wanted to see her happy.
All of those were true, but they felt slightly different.
“Still, I didn’t want to give up on the impossible.”
“I understand! I didn’t want to give up either!”
“Yeah—”
The fact that she had sent me so many notifications was proof that Sayori hadn’t given up.
“Hey, hey! Can I put all the chips on!?”
“Of course. That’s what I made them for.”
In fact, I would be troubled if she didn’t wear them.
Sayori began to snap each chip onto her fingers one by one. Though her expression was serious, her tail was wagging side to side like a dog, so it was clear she was overjoyed.
“This color... is it glitter?”
“No, it’s a metallic color. I could only use paint for plastic...”
“It turns out so beautifully gradient!”
“That’s thanks to the airbrush...”
For the design, I referenced several nails I found online and used the paints I had in the garage.
The tips were a light pink, gradually transitioning to a deeper metallic red toward the base of the nails. They were small parts, but with an airbrush, such gradients were possible.
As a finishing touch, I added gold paint with a detail brush for accent.
Well—considering it was my first attempt at nails, I thought it turned out pretty well.
“...Beautiful.”
After putting the nail chips on all her fingers, Sayori murmured that softly.
She spread her fingers wide, holding them up to the ceiling light to check the shine of the nails.
Eventually, overwhelmed with emotion, she stood up from her chair and began to hop around.
“I’m glad.”
I didn’t need to see her tail to know. I felt relieved to see her so happy.
(I’m glad...)
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9vdyn9A.jpeg
I was confident in the quality of the nail chips. Considering the process from shaping to finishing, it felt like I had made a slightly different kind of model.
But whether that would make Sayori happy was still uncertain.
Seeing her literally jump for joy made me truly happy.
(Is this what it feels like to create something for someone else?)
As I let out a sigh of relief at an emotion I had never known while making models alone—
“Azuma-kun! Thank you so much! I never thought it would be done so quickly!”
In the momentum of her hopping.
Sayori hugged me.
“Wha—! Y-You, let go!”
I felt something soft against my body.
I didn’t know what the scent was, but it smelled good. I hurriedly tried to pull away.
“Ahaha! Sorry! I just got so excited!”
Don’t hug a guy just because you’re excited.
I couldn’t forget the feeling of Sayori’s ample body when she hugged me. Being a model, her figure was too good, and it was a bit overwhelming.
“W-Well, I’m glad.”
“Yeah!”
The dragon girl smiled widely.
Sayori really suited that look, laughing as if she had no worries at all.
(It was a bit of an unusual creation, but... well, I guess this is the end.)
I stretched my body. After days of working, I was feeling stiff.
Originally, someone like me, an introvert, and someone like Sayori, a dragon girl, lived in different worlds. It just happened that nails became our connection, allowing us to talk like this—but...
I probably wouldn’t see her again after this. We exchanged contact information, but once the nail project was over, Sayori wouldn’t contact me again.
That would be just right.
I felt a little lonely about it, but—
“So, what should we make next?”
“Huh?”
I made a strange sound at her unexpected words.
“Next... what do you mean?”
“Eh? Well, I’m super happy about the nail chips, but we still haven’t painted the important polish!”
“W-Wait, isn’t nail art a one-time thing!?”
“No, no, no, no! That’s not how it works! Azuma-kun, you’re so funny!”
She laughed heartily.
“Because I want to do both polish and gel! I have to change my nails to match my outfits, and I want nails for photoshoots and my favorite nails too!”
“Wait, wait...”
“Oh, I could match my nails with my friends! Anyway, I want to do all sorts of nails to match my TPO! And also! —In any case, nails have infinite possibilities!”
While showing off her newly adorned nails.
“Azuma-kun, let me tell you something good♪”
“Huh?”

“Girls, you know, look at their own hands and the hands of others a lot! That’s why nails are a super important fashion that’s always in view. Makeup and fashion can only be seen in the mirror, but with nails, you can always look at your hands and think, ‘I’m cute!’”
Is that really true...?
I looked at the models lined up on the shelf. Indeed, seeing my own creations displayed always made me feel good.
Is that how it is?
“If there’s only one design, it’s going to be a downer! It’s like having only one outfit!”
“Y-Yeah, I get it...”
It might indeed feel lonely if there was only one model in the showcase.
—But is that analogy really correct?
“So, we’re going to do all sorts of things! Oh, of course, I’ll do my research too! I won’t make you do all the work, but—still.”
Sayori looked straight at me.
“You’re my personal nail artist now. I absolutely, definitely won’t let you go! So be prepared!”
—It seems that.
Without even realizing it, I might have taken on a big responsibility. I would have to create nails with Sayori to keep her excitement up.
“...I got it.”
Although I had no connection with the dragon girl before, now that I had become her personal nail artist, it seemed this connection wouldn’t easily fade away.
Having been appointed, I would have to use my skills and strive for mutual understanding.
I didn’t know how far I could go, but if I could see Sayori’s smile the moment she got her nails done, that would be a pretty good reward.
“Yeah, I’m looking forward to it, my nail artist!”
As Sayori tried to hug me again, I hurriedly stopped her.
—Reconsidering my previous statement. I really couldn’t believe that this dragon girl, with this kind of distance, was the same species as me, an introvert.
